captive_summary: No on-site captive gas power found. The terminal built and energized its own 110kV substation drawing power from the public grid, and its ORV vaporizers are heated by waste-heat seawater piped in from the adjacent, separately-owned, coal-fired Pinghai power station -- a heat inflow, not captive electric generation, and not the terminal's own plant.
confirmed_how: A construction-completion report (建筑时报, 2024-10-24) on the Huizhou LNG receiving station's build-out lists '110千伏变电所一次性受电成功' (the 110kV substation successfully received grid power on first energization) among the completed works -- the standard signature of a grid-connected industrial consumer, not an on-site generator. No source found in this pass mentions any on-site gas turbine or generator at the terminal itself. Separately, the terminal sits immediately north of Guangdong Huizhou Pinghai power station (per the 2021 provincial EIA approval, read via Read tool but not verifiable through url_verifier -- see log) -- that plant is confirmed coal-fired (chinadaily.com.cn, openinframap.org), an unrelated merchant plant on the same peninsula, and its role at the terminal (per other reporting) is supplying ORV vaporizer waste-heat seawater, i.e. heat flowing INTO the terminal, analogous to the settled Gate<-Uniper case -- not captive power in either direction.
